decisive_items: a tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast with overlying warmth, erythema
a skin fistula developed with pus extruding and an “orange peel” appearance of the overlying skin
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls throughout the gland, extending to the skin, with peripheral enhancement
response.rationale: Parous woman with negative infectious workup, enlarging inflammatory breast mass, fistula, and MRI ring-enhancing multifocal lesions is most consistent with idiopathic granulomatous lobular mastitis; R2 is the broader granulomatous mastitis category, while R1 is typically subareolar and infection-associated.

rejected.why: Periductal mastitis is usually subareolar/nipple-centered, often infectious or smoking-related, and less consistent with this diffuse outer-quadrant multifocal MRI pattern and negative infectious workup.
